For negative logit offsets log(wᵢ), sampled softmax has negative mass M=Σᵢwᵢexp(sᵢ) and loss L=log(exp(s₊)+M)−s₊. With weights independent of s₊, |∂L/∂s₊|=M/(exp(s₊)+M): increasing M strengthens positive attraction even without better relative discrimination. Detached weights give negative gradients q·rᵢ, where q is that aggregate factor and rᵢ=wᵢexp(sᵢ)/M. This algebra separates pressure from allocation, consistent with the coupling analyzed in [Decoupled Contrastive Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06848).

Score-dependent weights can change both. Even mean-one weights increase M when positively correlated with exp(sᵢ); normalizing Σwᵢ does not preserve exponential mass. Unnormalized wᵢ=exp(βsᵢ) yields exp((1+β)sᵢ), sharpening negatives and making pressure sensitive to score offsets and scale. Differentiating through weights adds derivative terms; detaching them changes the optimization. Normalized exponential weights remove common-offset sensitivity of the weights, but retain scale sensitivity. [Robinson et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.04592) study controllable hardness; [Wang and Liu](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021/html/Wang_Understanding_the_Behaviour_of_Contrastive_Loss_CVPR_2021_paper.html) analyze temperature-dependent hardness penalties.

Proposed controlled ablations: baseline; mass-preserving hardness weighting, rescaling weights so Σwᵢexp(sᵢ)=Σexp(sᵢ); pressure-only weighting, assigning every negative the same multiplier matching the weighted method’s per-example M; and the full method. Detach normalization factors consistently, otherwise exact mass preservation can cancel the intended reweighting gradient. Compare constant, delayed, ramped and reversed schedules with matched cumulative pressure; include detached versus differentiable weights and fixed versus learned score scale. Hold candidates, seeds and training budget fixed. Track M/exp(s₊), positive-gradient magnitude, negative-gradient concentration, score norms and macro validation HR@10. These are proposed controls, not established recommendation results.
